evidence: ATTRIBUTION_GAP: NavierStokes.PeriodicPaper.breakdownStatement (NavierStokes/PeriodicPaperTheorem.lean:148): ∃ u p f K, CandidateProperties ν u p f K ∧ ¬ Nonempty (GlobalSmoothSolution ν f), with no uniqueness conjunct. Uniqueness: NavierStokes.PeriodicViscosityUniqueness.classical_uniqueness_on_Icc (NavierStokes/PeriodicViscosityUniqueness.lean:65).

I read p.125–126 and PeriodicPaperTheorem.lean:26–162. periodic_corollary proves, for every ν>0, ℤ³-periodic lifts (u,p,f) solving Navier–Stokes on (0,1) with zero datum, a time-compact smooth force, SpeedUnboundedAtOne (equivalent to the limsup, since slices are continuous), one compact K inside the open cube with tsupport ∩ closed cube ⊆ K (equivalent to supp ⊆ π(K): the tsupport is ℤ³-invariant and K+k misses the closed cube for k≠0), and no global smooth periodic competitor. The only gap is the uniqueness presupposed by "the solution", stated separately in classical_uniqueness_on_Icc. Auditor and both skeptics agree. I adopt the pairing skeptic's correction: the Comparator theorem is supporting, not part.

findings.summary: breakdownStatement asserts that some smooth periodic solution blows up at t=1. It has no clause saying this is 'the' solution. The uniqueness the paper presupposes is a separate Lean theorem.
